SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.claim: The fire passage describes its condition without threatening to remove it: people can live without fire, but not without food or water.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.anchor: لأن الناس يمكن أن يعيشوا بلا نار لكن لا يمكنهم أن يعيشوا بلا طعام أو ماء

DAMGHANI:v1p468/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r8.claim: Nār can mean the fire concealed in flint, struck from the flint.
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r8.anchor: السادس النار الكامنة في الزناد قوله تعالى في سورة الواقعة أفرأيتم النار التي تورون يعني تقدحون من الزناد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p89/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p89/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p89/r8.claim: The tree is the wood from which fire is struck; construing the tree itself as fire is an unnecessarily strained metaphor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p89/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن شجرتها، المراد منه الشجر الذي يقدح منه النار

NAHHAS:v4p341/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
NAHHAS:v4p341/r2.claim: Some say seeing it means seeing with the eyes; Abu Jaʿfar rejects this, deriving the verb from kindling a firestick.
NAHHAS:v4p341/r2.anchor: قال بعض العلماء أي ترونها بأبصاركم قال أبو جعفر وهذا غلط ولو كان كما قال

ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r2.claim: Tūrūna means you kindle or strike a fire: the fire drill catches, while awraytu means I caused the fire to ignite; Arabs rubbed two sticks together to make fire.
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r2.anchor: تقول وري الزند يري وريا، فهو وار إذا انقدحت منه النار

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r17.claim: The fire people kindle is produced by rubbing materials together, an instance of fire generated by friction and contact.
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r17.anchor: birbirine sürtüp çakmak suretiyle çıkardığınız ateşi ki delk ü temas ile çıkan bir elektrik ateşi demektir.

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r18.claim: He links the fire from the tree to Yā Sīn 36:71.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r1.claim: Questions about human creation and familiar resources—rain and fresh water from salty seas, crops, and useful fire—invite reflection on their creator's will and power and on the human duty of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r1.anchor: İnsanın kendi varlığı ve yakın çevresinde her gün yararlandığı imkânlar üzerinde, bütün bu varlık ve oluşların hangi irade ve gücün eseri olduğu hakkında düşünmeye çağıran çarpıcı sorularla Allah Teâlâ’nın irade ve yaratma gücüne

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.claim: After creation and allotted death as preparation for resurrection and recompense, God cites crops, water, and fire, the three chief necessities of worldly life, to establish His lordship as governance rooted in ownership.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r1.anchor: عد لهم أمورا ثلاثة من أهم ما يعيشون به في الدنيا وهي الزرع الذي يقتاتون به والماء الذي يشربونه

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r8.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains al-iraʾ as producing fire by striking flint: one says the strike ignited when fire appeared, and akba when it did not.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r8.anchor: قال في المجمع الإيراء إظهار النار بالقدح، يقال أورى يوري

TABRISI:56:65-74/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:65-74/r13.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:56:65-74/r13.claim: They say fire is a reminder of the greater Fire, so whoever sees it remembers Hell and seeks God’s protection.
TABRISI:56:65-74/r13.anchor: نحن جعلنا هذه النار تذكرة للنار الأخرى الكبرى فإذا رآها الرائي ذكر جهنم واستعاذ بالله منها عن عكرمة ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:56:65-74/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:56:65-74/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:56:65-74/r14.claim: Another explanation makes the fire a prompt to reflect: the One who produces it from a green tree can bring about a second creation.
TABRISI:56:65-74/r14.anchor: معناه تذكرة يتذكر بها ويتفكر فيها فيعلم أن من قدر عليها وعلى إخراجها من الشجر الرطب قدر على النشأة الثانية

SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r1.claim: تورون means to strike a firestick and draw out its flame; the intransitive form means that its fire comes forth.
SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r1.anchor: من أوريت الزند أي: قدحته فاستخرجت ناره، ووري الزند يري أي: خرجت ناره

SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:71/r2.claim: The form تورون originally derives from توريون.

ASAD-NOTES:56:71/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:71/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:56:71/r1.claim: People kindle fire, but God asks whether they or He brought its fuel tree into being.
ASAD-NOTES:56:71/r1.anchor: tree that serves as its fuel [23] - or are We the cause

QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#1/r1.claim: The hmz reading softens the second hamza by replacing it with vowel lengthening; standard Ḥafṣ retains both hamzas.
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza softening: second hamza replaced by vowel lengthening; standard Ḥafṣ retains both hamzas

QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#2/r1.claim: The hmz variant replaces hamza with alif-madd, further smoothing the double-hamza sequence.
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#2/r1.anchor: Hamza replaced by alif madd — further phonetic smoothing of the double-hamza sequence

QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#3/r1.speaker: Cs
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#3/r1.claim: The Cs reading completely deletes hamza through tashīl; this attested canonical form removes the glottal interruption.
QIRAAT-ER:56:71:2#3/r1.anchor: Complete hamza deletion (tashīl) — attested canonical variant; reduces the glottal interruption entirely

ALUSI-FULL:v27p149#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p149#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p149#5/r1.claim: The fire is the one you kindle and draw out from the fire-sticks.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r6.claim: The fire is what people kindle and draw out from their fire-stick.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r10.claim: The Prophet said the fire people kindle is one part out of seventy of Hellfire; Hellfire exceeds it by sixty-nine parts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "نار بني آدم التي يوقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم"

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r7.claim: تورون means striking fire and producing sparks.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r3.claim: The question asks people to inspect with eyes and insight the particular fire they kindle, so they recognize God’s power through an unexpected created sign.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r3.anchor: أي أخبروني هل رأيتم بالأبصار والبصائر ما تقدم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r4.claim: The fire is struck from a firestick, whether dry or green; it is hidden in the wood until extracted, surprising anyone who has not tried it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r4.anchor: أي تستخرجون من الزند فتوقودون به سواء كان الزند يابسا أو أخضر بعد أن كانت خفية فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r5.claim: The hidden fire’s emergence evokes tawriya, where one thing appears while another is intended; the concealed flame then manifests with great power.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420/r5.anchor: فكان ذلك مثل التورية التي يظهر فيها شيء ويراد غيره , ثم صار بعد ذلك الخفاء إلى ظهور عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r1.claim: Fire exists in every tree, but people use markh and afar because they kindle especially easily; a cited saying says fire is in every tree, but these two are best.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r1.anchor: في كل شجر نار واستمجد المرخ والعفار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r5.claim: The discourse moves from water to fire as it earlier moved from crops and trees to water; fire comes from trees by striking them together and wood also fuels it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r5.anchor: ومناسبة الانتقال من الاستدلال بخلق الماء إلى الاستدلال بخلق النار هي ما تقدم في مناسبة الانتقال إلى خلق الماء من الاستدلال بخلق الزرع والشجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r6.claim: The fire drill's extraction of fire from apparently dead sticks makes resurrection imaginable: fire is brought out of lifeless rubbing wood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r6.anchor: وهذا استدلال على تقريب كيفية الإحياء للبعث من حيث إن الاقتداح إخراج والزند الذي به إيقاد النار يخرج من أعواد الاقتداح وهي ميتة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r7.claim: The description of kindling also embeds a reminder of God's favor, as in the preceding argument about drinking water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r7.anchor: وفي قوله : { التي تورون } إدماج للامتنان في الاستدلال بما تقدم في قوله : { أفرأيتم الماء الذي تشربون } ( الواقعة : 68 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r8.claim: The intended fire is the spark produced from a fire drill, not the resulting flame; the pronoun in شجرتها refers to fire, meaning the kind of wood used to kindle it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r8.anchor: وهو أيضا وصف للمقصود من الدليل وهو النار التي تقتدح من الزند لا النار الملتهبة . وضمير شجرتها عائد إلى النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r10.claim: تورون is the present of أورى الزند, rubbing one fire stick against another to draw out flame; the upper stick is the زند or زناد and the lower is the زندة.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r10.anchor: مضارع أورى الزند إذا حكه بمثله يستخرج منه النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r11.claim: Dhu al-Rumma takes up the same idea in an enigmatic description of kindling fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p325/r11.anchor: وقد تابع ذو الرمة هذا المعنى في وصفه الاقتداح للنار فقال على شبه الإلغاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r1.claim: The relative pronoun’s object return is omitted, a common deletion of accusative pronouns in relative clauses; the implied form is “which you kindle.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r1.anchor: وحذف العائد على الموصول لأن ضمير النصب يكثر حذفه من الصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r2.claim: “Kindle the fire” elliptically means kindle its tree, as the following verse makes clear; Arabic commonly omits this genitive complement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r2.anchor: وتعدية { تورون } إلى ضمير { النار } تعدية على تقدير مضاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r5.claim: Tūrūn means striking fire from firesticks; Arabs made these from stones, stone and iron, or suitable soft woods such as marḫ and ʿafār.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r5.anchor: و: تورون معناه: تقتدحون من الأزند، تقول أوريت النار من الزناد.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r8.speaker: الجمهور وأبو عمرو وعيسى وأبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r8.claim: Most readers lengthen the initial hamza in āntum; Abu Amr and Isa are also reported with a short hamza, which Abu Hatim deemed weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «آنتم» بالمد، وروي عن أبي عمرو وعيسى: «أنتم» بغير مد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses turuna as extracting or kindling fire, from awraytu, though wariytu is more commonly said.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة تستخرجون من أوريت وأكثر ما يقال وريت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the verse refers to fire extracted from fire-sticks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة التي تستخرجون من الزنود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says turuna means striking fire, as when one says awraytu al-nar for kindling it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج تورون أي تقدحون تقول أوريت النار إذا قدحتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541/r3.claim: The fire people kindle is struck from fire-sticks and drawn out of its source.

BURSEVI:v9p273/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273/r6.claim: Tūrūnah means kindling fire, bringing it out with a fire-drill; Arabs rubbed two sticks, calling the upper one zand and the lower one zandah.
BURSEVI:v9p273/r6.anchor: أي تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد والعرب تقدح بعودين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r1.claim: Tūrūna means striking fire and drawing it from firesticks; Arabs rub two sticks, calling the upper one the male and the lower one the female, by analogy with mating cattle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r1.anchor: تقدحونها وتستخرجونها من الزناد والعرب تقدح بعودين تحك أحدهما على الآخر ، ويسمون الأعلى : الزند ، والأسفل : الزندة ؛ شبهوهما بالفحل والطروقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r3.claim: The fire people kindle is extracted with a fire drill from wood, iron, or stone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r3.anchor: أي تستخرجون بزنادكم من شجر أو حديد أو حجر

MUQATIL:56:68-73/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r4.claim: The fire is that people kindle from wood, stones, and reeds, except al-anab.
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r4.anchor: يعنى توقدون من الشجر والحجارة والقصب إلا العناب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r1.claim: Tūrūn means that you kindle the fire and draw it from the firesticks.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r2.claim: Arabs make fire by rubbing two sticks: the upper is the male firestick and the lower the female, likened to a stallion and its mate.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#3/r2.anchor: والعرب تقدح بعودين تحك احداهما على الآخر ويسمون الأعلى الزند والاسفل الزندة شبهوهما بالفحل والطروقة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r5.claim: The fire is kindled by striking damp wood.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r5.anchor: أي أخبروني عن النار التي تظهرونها بالقدح من الشجر الرطب

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r6.claim: The tinder trees are markh and ʿafār; a proverb says every tree contains fire and these two abound in it and ignite readily.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r6.anchor: وهي المرخ والعفار ومنه قولهم: في كل شجر نار، واستمجد المرخ والعفار

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r7.claim: Awraytu means to kindle by striking; warā al-zand yarī describes a firestone producing sparks, with another pronunciation in the verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r7.anchor: يقال: أوريت النار إذا قدحتها. وورى الزند يرى إذا انقدح منه النار.

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r1.claim: One proposed tree is the species, such as marakh, from which fire is kindled with a fire drill.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r1.anchor: أنها الشجرة التي تورى النار منها بالزند والزندة كالمرخ

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r2.claim: Another proposal is any tree suitable as fuel: fire catches on wood more readily than on other things, making ignition possible.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r2.anchor: الشجرة التي تصلح لإيقاد النار كالحطب فإنها لو لم تكن لم يسهل إيقاد النار

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r3.claim: A third proposal identifies the tree with the sources and fuel of its flames; flames make it capable of cooking things.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#3/r3.anchor: أصول شعلها ووقود شجرتها ولولا كونها ذات شعل لما صلحت لإنضاج الأشياء

THALABI:v9p216/r24.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p216/r24.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p216/r24.claim: The fire is what people kindle and bring out from their fire-stick; God, not people, created the tree from which they kindle it.
THALABI:v9p216/r24.anchor: أفرأيتم النار التي تورون تقدحون وتستخرجون من زندكم أأنتم أنشأتم شجرتها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#3/r1.claim: Tūrūn means that you extract fire from the firestrikers.
